summary: Skamania County, WA two-story L-4 cab on Mount Mitchell (Siouxon Block, DNR); removed or destroyed 1970; road to the official trail blocked, so check access first.

facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1970 (sources differ); a footing is photographed at the summit with no date

staffing.status: Forest Service first, then Washington DNR until 1966

access.note: The main road to the official trail is blocked by private property issues; the Willhite page describes an unofficial trail and says the roads are poorly signed. Check with the Washington DNR before going.

facts.agency: Gifford Pinchot National Forest / Washington Dept. of Natural Resources

events.note: L-4 cab on the summit by 1942; construction date unknown (Willhite)
Aircraft Warning Service use, March 16, 1942 to October 16, 1943; sleeping quarters and a woodshed added
Two-story L-4 cab built in 1957 to replace an earlier emergency lookout (register); Willhite says the date is unclear
Former DNR lookout recalls a significant lightning bust centered on the lookout that summer
DNR staffing until 1966 per the register
Discontinued and replaced by air patrols; to be kept as a supply cache (Forest Lookouts quoting The Oregonian, August 18, 1969)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the two-story L-4 cab to 1957, replacing an earlier emergency lookout. Willhite finds an L-4 cab by 1942 with no known build date, and a former lookout recalls the Forest Service building it circa 1933. The 1957 date is also unclear per Willhite.

The register says removed in 1970; the inventory and firelookout.com say destroyed in 1970. A former lookout recalls it was burned as a fire hazard, with no date given. A 1969 report said it would be kept as a supply cache.

notes_for_editor: Build date and fate conflict across sources (see resolved_conflicts). The burning account is a secondhand recollection with no date, so it is not an event. The footing photo has no date. Access is restricted per the Willhite page (road to the official trail blocked); the story describes the unofficial trail the page mentions. The register's FFLOS registration date (July 16, 2012) was not visible in the text read, so no fflos_registered event. Within the 6-read budget.
